newsitem.title: USA: Glenn announces U.S. Space Day in May.
newsitem.headline: Glenn announces U.S. Space Day in May.

text.p: Former astronaut John Glenn said on Thursday he was retiring from the U.S. Senate and marked the 35th anniversary of his orbit of the Earth by announcing a national Space Day in May to promote space exploration.

Glenn, now a Democratic senator from Ohio, became the first American to orbit Earth on Feb. 20, 1962. He made three orbits in five hours before his Mercury spacecraft landed in the Atlantic Ocean near the Bahamas.

"It's hard for me to believe that it's been 35 years," Glenn said at a ceremony in Washington. "I've recalled it so many times it seems to me, instead of 35 years, it was more like a month ago or 35 days ago.

"One of the more memorable things building up to my flight was a time when right at a lull in the communications, (astronaut) Scott Carpenter came on the intercom, just before launch, and said, 'God speed, John Glenn.' And those words still fill me with emotion to this day," he added.
"I think it's very appropriate that we have a day set aside each year for a space day, where we look forward to recounting all the advantages that we have brought back from space," Glenn said.
After the Space Day ceremony in Washington, Glenn flew to his home town in New Concord, Ohio, where he announced he would not run for re-election next year after four terms in the Senate.

Glenn and other organisers of Space Day on May 22 hope it will be marked by programmes in schools and communities across the country. They have established an internet site with news about space at www.spaceday.com.

Events planned in Washington include dedication of a statue of an astronaut and special exhibits at the National Air and Space Museum. Space Day will mark the anniversary of President John Kennedy's 1961 speech to Congress setting the goal of landing Americans on the Moon by the end of that decade. The first Moon landing took place on July 20, 1969.

Glenn, 75, was a Marine Corps fighter pilot in World War Two and the Korean War and become one of the first seven U.S. astronauts in 1959. His orbital flight came after sub-orbital missions by Alan Shepard and Virgil Grissom in 1961. After leaving the space programme he was elected to the Senate in 1974 and was re-elected three times.
